App details

Compass & Altimeter

Check direction, coordinates and altitude using the sensors available on your phone.

In the worksPlannedAndroid

What it’s for

A practical aid for checking direction and height outdoors. Magnetic direction comes from the phone’s sensors; true north is shown only when reliable location and magnetic correction data are available. GPS and barometric altitude stay clearly distinguished, with quality information.

Main features

  • Magnetic north and, with reliable data, true north.
  • Choose from five coordinate formats and copy them.
  • Separate GPS and barometric altitude readings.
  • See the data source, quality and available accuracy.

This app is being planned and is not yet available to download. The description presents its intended functions.

Features in detail

Direction, coordinates, pressure and altitude

Magnetic heading and true north

Hold the device to read its heading in degrees and one of 16 compass directions. Magnetic north uses available sensors. True north also needs reliable location and a valid correction for the difference between magnetic and geographic north; that difference is shown when available. Weak or disturbed sensing prompts calibration help.

Five coordinate formats and copying

With a valid location, choose decimal degrees (DD), degrees/decimal minutes (DMM), degrees/minutes/seconds (DMS), or UTM and MGRS grid references. Copy the selected form with its direction or grid labels for another app or note. Changing format represents the same place; missing location does not show an old fix as current.

GPS altitude and accuracy

Location altitude is labelled GPS and appears only when supplied by the fix. It refers to the Earth’s mathematical reference surface, not automatically sea level. Horizontal accuracy and available vertical accuracy are separate; absent accuracy is shown as unavailable, not zero uncertainty.

Pressure and calibrated barometric altitude

A working barometer shows pressure in hPa. Enter reference pressure or a known altitude to calculate barometric altitude; automatic reference needs reliable identified data. Set Zero shows relative height change and Reset Zero returns to the absolute reference. GPS and barometric heights remain separate, with source and quality labels.

Partial availability and privacy

Location permission is needed only for location-dependent features. Denying it leaves the magnetic compass and available barometer usable. Without a barometer, GPS altitude can still work; without valid true-north data, magnetic mode remains. Observation stops outside visible use; no route tracking or location history is kept.

North temporarily missing

Tap the About logo seven times for a playful compass needle that drifts then spins faster. Its message jokes that north cannot be found. The offline scene uses no real sensor or location and changes no measurement or setting.

Use, settings and availability

Offline use

The main functions are designed to work on your device without a JN86 account. Ads, purchases and external links may need internet.

Language, settings and help

Choose one of eight app languages and adjust the available settings. About provides privacy information and a link to voluntary JN86 support. Support does not unlock paid functions. Availability is shown below.

Ads and optional ad removal

All described functions are planned to be free, with banner ads and optional one-time Google Play ad removal. No subscription is planned. The purchase screen shows the actual local price; purchase restoration uses Google Play.

Availability

This app is being created. The features described here are planned; it is not yet available to download.
